narrative: Iran's weekend closure of the Strait of Hormuz and IRGC claims of maritime control set up a significant geopolitical risk premium for the USD and JPY at the Tokyo open. This geopolitical escalation coincides with hawkish Jackson Hole rhetoric from Fed Chair Warsh, which would support USD/JPY after it closed Friday at 160.04. The resulting 145bp SOFR/ESTR carry advantage and Warsh's focus on concerning price stability likely to weigh on EUR/USD, which finished Friday at 1.1587. AUD/CHF remains a critical bilateral theme (spread: 1.919%), where the AUD 1W avg outperformance of +1.295% (n=4) faces a reversal test on risk-off flows despite its 435bp carry lead over the lagging CHF (-0.623%, n=6). Markets await the RBNZ rate decision on Wednesday as the next key policy catalyst.
